**Test image key features:**
- Field-level view showing soybean rows in late season
- Plants yellowing/browning and dying along rows
- Some rows severely affected, background plants greener/healthier
- Dead leaves remaining attached to stems
- Progressive yellowing → brown death pattern

**Comparison summary:**
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Top-left reference panel shows nearly identical field pattern — rows of yellowing/dying plants alternating with healthier ones. Interveinal chlorosis on close-up leaves matches what appears on test image foliage.
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Bottom-left reference also shows dying rows alongside survivors, but Charcoal_Rot typically shows gray bleached stems with charcoal-dust specks — not distinguishable at field scale.
- **Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus**: Bottom-right panel shows field-level yellowing, but SDMV typically has mosaic pattern, not the progressive row-death seen here.
- **Phytophthora**: Plants wilt with attached leaves but usually in wetter conditions with chocolate-brown lower stem.
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Patches rather than row-by-row pattern.
- All leaf-spot diseases (Frogeye, Septoria, Cercospora, etc.) don't match — they show focal lesions, not whole-plant death at field scale.

The test image most closely matches **Sudden_death_syndrome** — the characteristic row pattern of interveinal yellowing progressing to brown death, with healthy plants visible in background, matches the SDS reference very well.
